conviction_note: The Q3 number lands against the company's own July guide ('slightly higher than Q2's EUR176m'). The move will come from the Q4 guide, and every input that has moved since July points against it: Spanish power and gas, nickel and therefore surcharges, and a peer saying European demand is flat. The positives (NAS's October base-price rise, a promised working-capital release) are smaller. The stock is already about 7% off its early-September level, so p_up sits only modestly below 50 (44) on abs 6.5: -0.78 scaled, against a findings sum of -1.2. The gap is because part of the macro is plainly in the price.

already_public.what: Q3 2026 guide: 'EBITDA for the third quarter of 2026 will be slightly higher than that of the second quarter' (Q2 adjusted EBITDA EUR176m), given with H1 results

Management said on the Q2 call that working capital would be cut in H2 and Q3 would see a reduction depending on nickel. Q2 FCF was -EUR65m and net debt EUR1.36bn (2.5x), with a target of about 2.0x by year end
No trading update, no Informacion Privilegiada and no revision of the outlook was found between 24 July and the print

new_in_release.expect: Q3 EBITDA roughly at the guide (~EUR176-185m). US strong; Europe hurt by the August shutdowns, weak demand and September energy costs. Slight miss is more likely than a beat (print_vs_bar -2%)
Q4 guide (Acerinox gives a next-quarter guide every quarter). Expect 'lower than Q3' on seasonality, energy and falling nickel surcharges. This is where the move is, and it leans negative
Working-capital release promised for H2. Lower nickel helps it. Leans positive versus Q2's -EUR65m FCF
Possible inventory adjustment on the nickel decline, which was excluded from adjusted EBITDA in Q4 2025 (EUR60m) and Q1 2026 (EUR25m). It would hit reported EBITDA, not the adjusted figure
unknown: any update on a US listing of the North American business (raised in May 2026); no filing found

findings.finding: Iberian energy spiked after the July guide, which never mentions energy. Spanish wholesale power averaged EUR143.3/MWh in September (highest month since 2022) and EUR159.4/MWh in the first ten days of October, more than double the EUR64.9 of the same period of 2025. MIBGAS gas was +143.5% y/y. Acerinox Europa's Los Barrios EAF and rolling mills are directly exposed, and peer Aperam put elevated energy costs at about EUR20m of EBITDA per quarter on 6 October.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The guide is what moved this name. Q2's beat plus a 'slightly higher' guide gave +10.7% on 2026-07-24. Q1 2026 (8 May) fell 1.96% despite a profit beat. Q2 2025 (24 Jul 2025) fell 4.73%
findings.original_quote: Septiembre cerró con una media de 143,3 €/MWh, el precio mensual más alto desde 2022 ... En los diez primeros días de octubre la media subió a 159,4 €/MWh. ... El MIBGAS, la referencia del gas en España, promedió 77,56 €/MWh en septiembre, un 143,5% más que en septiembre de 2025 (September closed at an average of EUR143.3/MWh, the highest monthly price since 2022 ... in the first ten days of October the average rose to EUR159.4/MWh ... MIBGAS averaged EUR77.56/MWh in September, 143.5% more than September 2025)
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: it is public macro, and ACX slid from about EUR18.3 (4 Sep) to EUR16.5-17.0 through October. But nobody has turned it into an Acerinox number, because the company has said nothing since July, so the size of the Q4 hit (hedges and PPAs, electro-intensive compensation) is unknown until the release. If it were fully priced, ACX would have fallen in step with the October power spike rather than bouncing +3% in five days. Macro-to-company transmission, so it is sized small.
findings.independence: Aperam's Q3 update (direct peer, 6 Oct 2026): 'Elevated energy costs are expected to weigh on EBITDA by about EUR20m per quarter' https://www.webdisclosure.com/press-release/aperam-update-on-q3-2026-market-financial-trends-WnJ6ONcR7SK ; daily OMIE 196.86 EUR/MWh on 26 Oct https://tarifaluzhora.es/precio-luz-diario/2026-10-26

findings.finding: Nickel kept falling after the July outlook. In July the company itself warned that 'the recent decline in nickel prices is expected to affect alloy surcharges and, consequently, transaction prices'. LME monthly averages went 17,064 (Jul), 16,701 (Aug), 15,738 (Sep) USD/t, with about 15,695 cash on 23 Oct. That means lower Q4 surcharges and prices, plus risk of an inventory adjustment like Q4 2025's EUR60m.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q4 2025 carried a EUR60m inventory adjustment and the FY print (27 Feb 2026) still closed +2.5%: the market looked through the adjustment line. The surcharge and price line feeds the next-quarter guide
findings.why_not_priced: LME nickel is public and watched. What is not priced is how far Acerinox passes the decline into the Q4 guide. The inventory adjustment sits outside adjusted EBITDA, so that part is sized at a fraction.

findings.finding: Aperam, the closest European peer, said on 6 October that European stainless 'underlying demand remains unchanged at a low level in Q3 2026' with no noticeable order-book improvement. It said the trade-defence benefit was largely pulled forward into H1. This cuts against Acerinox's July premise that the 1 July measures 'will help increase sales' in Europe.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Europe swung the H1 story: stainless EBITDA went from 82 to 154 and the stock rose +10.7% on 24 Jul 2026. A Europe disappointment is the main downside channel for the guide
findings.why_not_priced: It is a peer statement three weeks old, and Aperam's own guide had already said Q3 would be below Q2. Partly priced, sized small. It is net of the US business (about half of revenue), which this does not touch. The Aperam document is shared with finding 1, but the facts differ (demand vs energy).
findings.independence: Fastmarkets/Eurometal: North European 304 CR prices flat month on month in early October (date not verified, so not load-bearing) https://eurometal.net/european-stainless-steel-prices-steady-amid-uncertainty-over-safeguard-review-cbam/

findings.finding: North American Stainless (Acerinox's US arm, the group's main profit driver) announced base-price increases effective with 1 October 2026 shipments. The functional discount narrows by 2 points on 316 CR and 4 points on 430 CR, and round bar in 17-4/416/410 rises USD0.075/lb. That is evidence of US pricing power going into Q4.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The July outlook leaned on 'the strength of the U.S. market', and that guide produced +10.7%
findings.why_not_priced: A US mill price letter is trade-press material, not wire copy, and it covers only some grades (not 304). Small, partly offset by falling nickel surcharges.
findings.independence: ChemAnalyst: US stainless flat prices 'remain firm in August 2026' on infrastructure and data-centre demand https://www.chemanalyst.com/NewsAndDeals/NewsDetails/us-stainless-steel-flat-prices-remain-firm-in-august-2026-44106

findings.finding: After Q2's -EUR65m FCF and EUR1.36bn net debt disappointed, management promised an H2 working-capital cut, with the Q3 reduction depending on nickel. Nickel has since fallen about 8% from the July average, which mechanically lowers inventory value. So Q3 operating cash flow and net debt should improve, against a year-end target of about 2.0x.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2's cash and debt miss came on a day the stock rose +10.7%, so the earnings line dominated. Cash is secondary on this name but a check against a guide cut
findings.why_not_priced: It was guided, so it is mostly expected. The size depends on nickel, which has moved since. Sized small. Not a contradiction with finding 2: lower nickel cuts prices and frees working capital at the same time.
findings.independence: Quartr Q2 call summary: 'Targeting a debt/EBITDA ratio of around 2 by year-end' https://quartr.com/events/acerinox-s-a-acx-q2-2026_3ePYKrdt

baseline_tension: The findings lean negative on the Q4 guide. That agrees with the 60-day run-up (-6.9%) and cuts mildly against the 5-day bounce (+3.0%). The 20-day lean (+0.03) is flat, so the findings are mostly orthogonal to the free control. Because part of the energy and nickel macro is visibly in the price, p_up is held at 44 rather than lower.
language_note: Spanish energy-market press (roams.es, citing OMIE and Grupo ASE) carried the hard numbers on the Iberian power and gas spike (Sept EUR143.3/MWh, MIBGAS +143.5% y/y). No English stainless or Acerinox source connected this to Acerinox.

Renta 4's Spanish note carried the explicit statement that the Q3 guide is 'en linea con nuestras estimaciones' and the 'impacto positivo superior al 5%' call on Q2. English wires carried only 'beat'.
On company facts (guide, cash, nickel warning), nothing the English sources did not already carry.
lessons_applied: 'The move is in the guide' and 'too small about the move': abs_move_pct raised from 5.5 to 6.5. A Q4 guide is a scheduled guidance event on new numbers (base 7-9%), discounted somewhat for a liquid 14-analyst name. expected_move_pct goes from -0.66 to -0.78.
'Cash can outweigh a raised guide': the working-capital finding was checked and kept at +0.4, not changed.
Macro-to-company transmission: the energy finding was already sized with that caveat in place (peer quantified, company silent), so it was not shrunk a second time.
